title: User-Regulation Deconfounded Conversational Recommender System with Bandit Feedback

problem.claim: Conversational recommender systems can produce biased recommendations when conversational key-terms introduce biases and key-term-level preferences are overrated relative to the item itself.

gap.claim: Existing traditional debiasing methods are not designed to model item-key-term preference relationships and do not effectively measure potentially useful biases conveyed through conversational key-terms.

contributions.claim: The abstract concerns handling bias arising from the relationship between items and conversational key-terms in conversational recommender systems.

narrative_sequence.summary: Conversational recommender systems have achieved success in addressing the cold-start problem.
Conversational key-terms help elicit preferences but can introduce bias, causing systems to favor overrated key-terms over items.
Bias from item-key-term relationships needs to be handled because key-term conversation is central to these systems.
Traditional debiasing approaches focus on item or item-group re-ranking or re-weighting and do not model or measure useful conversational key-term biases effectively.

source_observation.claim: A preference signal used to improve cold-start recommendation can also introduce bias when the signal is modeled independently of the item.

interpretation.claim: Conversational preference elicitation should account for relationships between preference cues and the items they describe.

application.claim: When designing conversational recommendation systems, evaluate and regulate key-term-related bias rather than relying only on item-level debiasing.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether regulating key-term bias improves recommendation performance in specific settings.

unknowns: The proposed system design and bandit-feedback mechanism are not described.
No datasets, baselines, metrics, numerical results, or experimental conditions are provided.
The abstract does not specify how useful biases are measured or regulated.
